title: Check regression discrimination in every claimed dtype and path
applies_when: A padding, masked-content or warm-cache regression test compares paired outputs across FP16/BF16 dtypes or execution paths; broad tolerances or an omitted empty-prefix sentinel transition can hide a defect. Recovery after a generation-context exception may preserve finite loss while breaking nonpersistent weight release. Upstream drift may partially repair an older bug while its broad regression turns green without covering the remaining path.
lesson: Execution success and regression discrimination are different evidence. Run identical test bytes on the known-bad parent and repair, and inspect each claimed affected dtype/path separately; legitimate unchanged controls may pass in both. Establish the real consumer contract before changing assertions. For deterministic paired calls where only ignored masked content differs, exact output invariance can be appropriate even when kernel/reference comparisons need tolerances. In FLA SimpleGLA PR #1273, real RTX5090 layer/Triton calls gave parent 2 failed/2 passed and candidate 4 passed: both BF16 regressions already passed at tolerance 0.02. Repeating the same constructions with paired torch.equal made all four regressions fail before and pass after, with exact repaired output invariance; three related caller controls passed after. Use this to assess the oracle, not to manufacture a baseline failure. Also inspect cached state sentinels, not just perturbed payloads: LightNet's all-padding prefix leaves log-normalizer=-inf and recurrent state=0. Its first valid token can produce a -inf reset gate that fused recurrence tolerates but chunk cumulative differences turn into NaN. Check empty/nonempty prefixes and short/chunk continuations, finite output/state and masked-input gradients; matching the existing prefill nonfinite-gate policy depends on the zero-state invariant. For resource recovery, assert the configured lifecycle postcondition as well as numeric output: a missing ZeRO-3 post-forward hook can retain full nonpersistent weights even when a caught generation exception is followed by finite loss and a successful training step. Pair normal and exceptional exits, disable parameter reuse/prefetch when requiring immediate release, and check before backward/step could hide the retained allocation.
avoid_when: Do not require every control or unaffected cell to fail on the parent. Exact paired invariance is not a universal bitwise policy for stochastic calls, gradients, different reduction schedules, kernel/reference comparisons or different devices. The SimpleGLA observation covers small layer cases with use_short_conv=False, not backward or full-model behavior. LightNet's zero-state sentinel rule is not a general license to replace nonfinite gates or relax numerical budgets. The selected RTX5090 tests do not establish other backends, supported varlen, a full model backward matrix, performance or overall upstream readiness. Available advice and these development cases do not demonstrate better Scout conversion or lower total research cost. Do not demand zero-sized weight storage when persistence, reuse or prefetch legitimately retains it; this is a configured resource contract, not a general implementation invariant. The cited DeepSpeed fork commit defines a focused regression and proposed repair, not an accepted upstream PR or public full-model/OOM/performance qualification.

evidence.note: After main c127deb9 gained a context-error guard, the original native S3 SDK regression passed all three race-enabled repeats even though the uninterruptible retry delay remained. The strengthened test deterministically cancels immediately after observing a nil Err and asserts no extra List call: unchanged main fails the backoff cell in all three repeats, while exact repair 7731296e1 passes. Object-package tests excluding the known root-permission TestDisk2 failure and go vet pass; not full make test.pkg, live cloud, performance or prospective Scout utility. Recheck old tests on current main before resolving PR conflicts, retain upstream guards/logs, and discriminate the residual contract rather than manufacturing timing thresholds.

The exact PR tests cover interior padding and warm-cache continuation in FP16/BF16 with paired masked-content perturbations. These source bytes define the cases, not independent GPU execution evidence.

Independent real-layer/Triton validation of exact head 5fd4d711 against parent 954438d1 on RTX5090, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0 and Python 3.12.13. Original BF16 checks pass before repair despite relative errors 0.008699/0.014372; deterministic paired equality discriminates all four cells. No monkeypatch, performance or full-suite claim.

Cached-padding repair with 22 registered FP16/BF16 layer cases, including empty-prefix short/chunk forward and backward, plus 10 selected caller/config/generation controls: 32 passed on RTX5090/Torch 2.11/Triton 3.6. Public diff shows the prefill-policy reuse and zero-state precondition. H100/Torch 2.12/Triton 3.7.1 smoke subsequently failed with illegal memory access in the T=80 backward case. A cold-cache RTX5090/Torch 2.11 diagnostic with Triton 3.7.1 and synchronous CUDA launches passed all eight selected gradient cases, but H100/Torch 2.12 root cause remains unresolved. Isolating one compiler-version change does not reproduce another architecture/runtime combination. Local success is not cross-architecture qualification, a prospective policy comparison or a performance claim.

Public two-file fork repair puts training-hook restoration in finally. Its real ZeRO-3 train/context/train regression compares normal versus ValueError exit and checks nonpersistent weight release with reuse and prefetch disabled. Source/test evidence only; no upstream acceptance, full-suite, OOM or speedup claim.
